The quiet economics of newsletters

Most writers earn less than you think, and that is fine

Every few months someone posts a screenshot of a newsletter dashboard with a six-figure number on it, and every few months a few hundred writers quit their jobs.

I have run this newsletter for four years. Here is what the numbers actually look like for a writer with 11,000 free readers and about 600 paying ones.

Where the money comes from

  1. Annual plans make up 70 percent of revenue.

  2. Monthly plans churn at about 4 percent a month.

  3. Founding members are rare but generous.

The surprise was how little the free list matters once it passes a few thousand. Conversion stays near 5 percent no matter how many people sign up, so growth is mostly about writing things people forward.

revenue = paid * price * (1 - fees)
fees    = 0.10 + card costs
